clue.text: Mass of junk mail replaced by text for brief periods

indicators.note: one letter of the junk-mail word is swapped out and the text abbreviation goes in its place

parts.note: spam is unsolicited email
M is the physics symbol for mass
SMS is a text message

explanation.surface: A heap of unwanted post giving way to text messages, for short spells.
explanation.walkthrough: In SPAM, the M (mass) is replaced by SMS, giving SPA + SMS.
explanation.definitionFit: Spasms are sudden short bursts of activity or feeling, so they can be brief periods.

clue.text: Type of plugs at bottom of list

parts.note: PR, public relations, gets things plugged
in can mean at, as in 'at home' and 'in'

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom is the final letter

explanation.surface: A kind of advert sits at the foot of a list.
explanation.definitionFit: Print means printed letters, as in 'small print', which is the same as type.

clue.text: Austerity that's new in author's son

indicators.note: the new letter goes inside the author's name and son

parts.note: Laurence Sterne wrote Tristram Shandy; 'author's' gives his name plus S
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Hard times are new in a writer's boy.
explanation.definitionFit: Austerity and sternness both mean severe strictness of manner.

clue.text: More than one 19 potentially from 2 & 14, 6 & 20 or 8 & 24

indicators.note: the letters could be made from the paired answers if they were rearranged

parts.note: 2 down's answer, print
14 down's answer, reasoners

explanation.surface: Plural bosses could arise from several pairings of other answers.
explanation.walkthrough: 19 across is BOSS. Each pair named (2 and 14, 6 and 20, 8 and 24) holds the same fourteen letters, so any of them is anagram fodder; the parse shows the first pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Senior partners run a firm, so they are bosses.

clue.text: Diffuse style rattled for most part

parts.note: a perm is a hairstyle

indicators.note: most of the word is kept: its final letter is dropped

parts.note: eaten (up), as in 'what's eating you?', means bothered or rattled

explanation.surface: A wordy style that has been thrown off balance in most places.
explanation.walkthrough: Rattled here means bothered, the sense in 'what's eating you?', so the past participle is the word cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: To diffuse through something is to spread right through it, the verb sense of permeate.

clue.text: Original top hunter chap is … me?

definitions.text: Original top hunter chap is … me?

indicators.note: the words are made into something original, a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An early man boasting that he is the first great hunter.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition as well: the ape-man speaks, claiming to be the original hunter.
explanation.definitionFit: Pithecanthropus was the name given to Java Man, an early human ancestor and so an original hunting man.

clue.text: Stop cats and dogs?

parts.note: a rest is a stop or pause
it rains cats and dogs in a downpour

explanation.surface: A request to halt the pets.
explanation.walkthrough: Pets on a leash are held back, so the whole clue defines the answer too.
explanation.definitionFit: To restrain is to hold back, as cats and dogs on a leash are.

clue.text: Sides knocked out in '70 World Cup, for example

indicators.note: the first and last letters are removed, leaving the inside

parts.note: the year '70 written as a word

explanation.surface: Teams eliminated from the 1970 football World Cup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sides' looks like football teams but means the edges of the word SEVENTY.
explanation.definitionFit: The World Cup is a sporting event, a competition or occasion.

clue.text: Land shred up by reptiles

parts.note: terra is Latin for land

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: to snip is to cut into pieces

explanation.surface: Ground torn up by some lizards.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrapins are freshwater turtles, which are reptiles.

clue.text: Is inactive, killing bats in here

indicators.note: the letters of the following words are destroyed and remade in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone lazing about while killing bats in this place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Killing bats' looks like vermin control, but 'killing' is the anagram signal for BATS IN HERE.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal that hibernates spends the winter dormant, which is being inactive.

clue.text: What followed punt inside of nervous cell

indicators.note: only the inner letters are kept, with both ends removed

parts.note: a neuron is a nerve cell

explanation.surface: A boating scene and a jittery cell from biology class.
explanation.walkthrough: The punt is not the boat but the Irish pound, replaced by this currency in 2002. NEURON loses its outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The euro replaced Ireland's old currency, the punt, so it is what came after it.

clue.text: Small sort of phaeton?

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

indicators.note: a rough sort of the following word, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking whether a carriage is a little kind of phaeton.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: S plus an anagram of PHAETON, and the answer is a light open carriage of the phaeton family.
explanation.definitionFit: A stanhope is a light one-seated open carriage, a variety of the horse-drawn phaeton.

clue.text: Knighted dramatist loosens tips of ivory and gold cane

indicators.note: the dramatist's name lets go of the named letters, which drop out

parts.note: Sir Terence Rattigan was an English playwright

indicators.note: the first letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A knighted playwright prising the ends off an ivory-and-gold walking stick.
explanation.walkthrough: RATTIGAN loses I and G, the tips of ivory and gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Rattan is the stem of a climbing palm used for canes and wickerwork.

clue.text: Let off majority of cold weather, but only just!

indicators.note: more than half of the word is kept
only just over half: four of the six letters stay and the last two go

parts.note: a freeze is a spell of icy weather

explanation.surface: Escaping most of a cold snap, by a whisker.
explanation.definitionFit: To free someone is to release them, the same as letting them off.

clue.text: They think those adding flavour should use pepper, ultimately, instead of a pinch of salt

indicators.note: the new letter is put to use in the word
the new letter takes the place of the old one

parts.note: seasoners add salt and pepper

indicators.note: a pinch is a tiny amount, so just the first letter of the word
at the end: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Advice to cooks: use pepper rather than a pinch of salt.
explanation.walkthrough: In SEASONERS, the S (a pinch of salt) is replaced by R (pepper, ultimately).
explanation.definitionFit: Reasoners are people who think things through logically.

clue.text: Perhaps Johnson, in a way, once backed by fools, according to the Speaker

indicators.note: the earlier pieces are supported from behind by what follows

parts.note: via is an old word for a way or road, from the Latin

indicators.note: the following word is given as it is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: tricks, as a verb, means fools or deceives

explanation.surface: A politician called Johnson, in some way, being supported by idiots, says the Speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: Johnson is not Boris but Amy Johnson, the pioneering 1930s pilot. The Speaker suggests Parliament but signals a sound-alike: TRICKS said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: Amy Johnson was a famous woman pilot, and aviatrix is the dated word for a female aviator.

clue.text: Banned professor's ulterior data provider

parts.note: tabu is a variant spelling of taboo, forbidden

indicators.note: how a plummy professor would say the word, a sound-alike

parts.note: ulterior can mean later or subsequent

explanation.surface: A banned academic's hidden motive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ulterior' suggests a hidden motive but here means later, said as an affected academic might.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabulator sets out figures in tables, so it provides information arranged neatly.

clue.text: See 4
Mum invested in banker behind revolutionary engine part

indicators.note: the quiet word is put inside the other pieces as if clothed in them

parts.note: a banker is a river (it has banks); the Cam flows through Cambridge
aft means at the back, as on a ship
keeping mum means staying silent, and SH is a call for silence

explanation.surface: A mother putting money into a bank behind a revolutionary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' looks like a reversal signal or Che, but it is part of the definition: the part rotates. The banker is the river through Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A camshaft is a rotating shaft carrying cams that open an engine's valves, so it turns as the engine runs.

clue.text: Behave like Victor Hugo?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to dominate, as a victor would
second meaning: Hugo ... is a German fashion house

explanation.walkthrough: Victor Hugo the novelist is a red herring: the two words are split, the first a winner, the second a designer label.
explanation.definitionFit: Boss as a verb means to lord it over others, and Hugo Boss is a clothing brand.

clue.text: Soul song's intro in Evita

indicators.note: the first letter goes inside the surname

parts.note: Eva Perón, the subject of Evita

indicators.note: the introduction, the first letter

explanation.surface: A soul number whose opening appears in the musical Evita.
explanation.walkthrough: Soul is not music but a person, as in 'not a soul'.
explanation.definitionFit: Soul in 'not a soul in sight' means a human individual.

clue.text: Actor and actress with hygiene problem first time

indicators.note: the hygiene problem is moved from the end of the actress's name to the front

parts.note: Greta Garbo, the Swedish film star
BO is body odour

explanation.surface: A film star and a co-star who suffered body odour for the first time.
explanation.walkthrough: GARBO ends in BO; putting it first gives BOGAR, then T. Humphrey Bogart was the Casablanca star.
explanation.definitionFit: Humphrey Bogart was a Hollywood film star, so he is an example of an actor.

clue.text: Before noon, I picked up José's mate

parts.note: am is ante meridiem, before noon

indicators.note: heard, as by a microphone: a sound-alike

parts.note: the ego is the I, the self

explanation.surface: A man rising before midday to pick up a Spanish friend.
explanation.walkthrough: José marks the answer as Spanish.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is Spanish for friend, a mate to someone such as José.

clue.text: Go back to forces on space series

parts.note: re means on or concerning
an en is a printer's space
a list is a series of items

explanation.surface: Returning to the military for a run of space missions.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-enlist is to sign up again for military service, going back to the armed forces.

clue.text: Bore any way but west

parts.note: a tedious thing, spelt out by the compass points other than west joined by 'or'

explanation.walkthrough: Any direction but west is south, north or east: S, N OR E spells the answer, which means a bore.
explanation.definitionFit: A snore, like a bore, is something tedious, as in 'what a snore'.

clue.text: Now essentially extinct mountain-dweller?

parts.note: yet can mean now, as in 'don't go yet'

indicators.note: at its core: the central letter of the word

explanation.surface: A creature living in the hills that is now all but extinct.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the yeti as a creature of legend.
explanation.definitionFit: The yeti is the legendary abominable snowman said to live in the Himalayas, hence a dweller on mountains.

clue.text: Stance against old hubby leaving child abandoned

indicators.note: the stance word sits up against, next to, the former husband

parts.note: an ex is a former husband
a position is a stance or attitude

explanation.surface: Taking a stand against a former husband who walked out on his child.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the rare sense of exposing an infant: leaving it out in the open to die.
explanation.definitionFit: Exposition can mean exposure, the old practice of abandoning an infant out of doors.

clue.text: Finds trouble in Walthamstow, E 17?

parts.note: the answer to 17 down is partners, and spouses are partners

explanation.surface: Someone in the London district of Walthamstow, postcode E17, gets into bother.
explanation.walkthrough: Trouble is rhyming slang: trouble and strife means wife, so to find trouble is to take a wife. Walthamstow's postcode is E17, which splits into E and 17 down.
explanation.definitionFit: To espouse is to marry, so it means finding yourself a wife.

clue.text: Ate last of pangolin boarded by Noah

indicators.note: the final letter of the following word

parts.note: jokily, something Noah took on board was 'arked'

explanation.surface: Someone eating the scaly anteater that Noah took on his ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ate' looks like eating, but it means bothered, as in 'what's eating you?'
explanation.definitionFit: Narked means annoyed or irritated, and to be eaten up by something is to be irritated.
